clue.text: Black and white photo's source that is obvious

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so the photo supplies only its opening letter

parts.note: i.e. (id est) is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'
bald, as in a bald statement, means plain and obvious

explanation.surface: A monochrome photograph whose origin is plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black and white' looks like a description of the photo, but it is the definition, of a horse's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has irregular patches of two colours, typically black and white.

clue.text: Day under pressure brings difficult situation

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece under another comes after it

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
daylight, or simply light, is the day as opposed to darkness

explanation.surface: A day spent under stress produces a tricky predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts LIGHT below P in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a dangerous or unfortunate predicament.

clue.text: Disclose gun with case removed

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so its first and last letters go

parts.note: a revolver is a handgun

explanation.surface: Reveal a weapon by taking it out of its holster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with case removed' takes the outer Rs from REVOLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense to evolve is to unfold or bring out what is wrapped up, close to revealing it.

clue.text: One whose origins can be traced back to Darwin?

definitions.text: One whose origins can be traced back to Darwin?

parts.words: One whose origins can be traced back to Darwin?
parts.note: Darwin is the capital of the Northern Territory, so someone born there comes from that country, not from evolution theory

explanation.walkthrough: 'origins' and 'Darwin' suggest Charles Darwin and the descent of species; the Darwin meant is the city in Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in the city of Darwin is a native of that country, so their origins trace back there.

clue.text: Object's mostly unassuming…

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: demure means modest and unassuming

explanation.surface: An item that is largely modest in appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a noun but is the verb. The ellipsis links it to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Romantic big day oddly ignored by lecturer Alice essentially

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second, fourth and sixth of these two words
the essence of a word is its core, so the name loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wedding day romance in which a lecturer called Alice gets left out of the celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' keeps IDY from 'big day'; 'essentially' gives LIC, the middle of Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic means picturesquely charming and idealised, the sense of a romantic, pastoral scene.

clue.text: …thereby a cost of perhaps tiny sum originally

indicators.note: originally says this piece comes at the start, before the other

parts.note: 1p, a single penny, is a tiny sum, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: modestly objecting to a cost of what might be a trifling amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 1p is one penny in British money, read as IP. 'perhaps' shuffles A COST OF to SOFACTO, and 'originally' puts IP first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, so it does the work of thereby in an argument.

clue.text: Reverse cart a short distance

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the word backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low, heavy cart for barrels

explanation.surface: Back a cart up a little way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' turns DRAY round.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is a unit of length of three feet, a short distance.

clue.text: City supporter setting up bar somewhere in Canada

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: in a down answer setting a word up means writing it bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a metal bar

explanation.surface: A city football fan sets up a bar somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City supporter' reads as a fan of Manchester City or similar; the city is Los Angeles. 'setting up' turns ROD round.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland region of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

clue.text: Vicar overlooks fool in church making crack

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that overlooks another sits above it

parts.note: Rev, for Reverend, is a vicar's title
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A vicar keeps an eye on an idiot in church, resulting in a joke or a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooks' means sits above, in a down entry; 'in' sets the pair inside the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier or ice sheet.

clue.text: On stage Jeremy presses clubs to expose West Ham United

definitions.meaning: Jeremy ... is the English stage and screen actor
to press clothes is to smooth them flat with a hot iron
in golf, the clubs with angled metal heads are called ...
West Ham United, the London football club, is nicknamed after the ironworks that founded it

explanation.surface: An actor puts pressure on football clubs to show up West Ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions in a row, linked by 'to expose'. West Ham United is a London football club whose nickname comes from its origins as the Thames Ironworks works team.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word serves as an actor's surname, a verb for smoothing clothes, golf clubs and a football club's nickname.

clue.text: Unhappy Lib Dem politician, in 2015 losing seat and pessimistic ultimately

indicators.note: losing says letters are taken away from the politician's title and name

parts.note: Vince Cable lost his Twickenham seat in 2015 and was then plain Mister Cable, not yet knighted

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letter of each of the two words before and after it

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat feels low after losing their seat at the 2015 election and growing gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T and C, the ends of 'seat' and 'pessimistic'; 'losing' takes them out of MISTER CABLE. Vince Cable, a Liberal Democrat MP, lost his seat in the 2015 UK general election before being knighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable is a direct synonym for wretched and sad, just as unhappy is.

clue.text: One going around sporting a puffy skirt when husband finished work

definitions.text: One going around sporting a puffy skirt

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogy tables
over means ended or finished
a craft is a skilled trade or line of work

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in a puffy skirt moves about once her husband's working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'puffy skirt' is not clothing: it is the inflated rubber skirt a hovercraft rides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovercraft travels over land and water on a cushion of air held in by a flexible skirt.

clue.text: Driver leaving Phoenix, first to accident, volunteers information

indicators.note: leaving says one word departs from the other, taking its letters away

parts.note: River Phoenix was the American film actor, so Phoenix stands for his first name

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A motorist drives away from Phoenix, Arizona, and the first on the scene of a crash offer details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phoenix' looks like the Arizona city; it is the actor River Phoenix, and 'leaving' takes RIVER out of 'Driver' to leave D. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference, a plain synonym of information.

clue.text: Ways to reach the next level? Actress is confused about answer

definitions.text: Ways to reach the next level?

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the single letter
confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeking promotion, an actress is unsure of the right response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ways to reach the next level' sounds like career advancement; it means the next floor. 'confused' shuffles ACTRESS IS and 'about' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Flights of steps are the literal way up from one floor of a building to the floor above.

clue.text: Disputes Conservative is blocking changes

indicators.note: a piece blocking a passage sits inside it, so the party letter goes inside the word for changes

parts.note: alterations are changes

explanation.surface: Arguments arise because a Tory is obstructing reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is blocking' puts C inside ALTERATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Altercations are noisy quarrels or arguments, so disputes is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Meat cooked with no oil is tender

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Meat prepared without oil comes out soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like a description of the meat; it means easily moved to feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender as in sensitive and easily moved matches the sense of being stirred by feelings.

clue.text: Train operator's ten hour disruption after beginning of strike

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters behind the single opening letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter
disruption means things thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rail company suffers ten hours of delays when a strike begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' signals the anagram and 'after' puts it behind S. Southern is a British rail operator south of London, notorious in 2016-18 for long strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Southern is the brand name of a British train operating company serving Sussex and south London.

clue.text: Exclusive college disheartened intellectuals over minute breach of etiquette

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed over another comes above it

parts.note: sole means exclusive, as in sole rights

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only its outer letters stay

explanation.surface: Snobbish college academics fret over a tiny lapse in manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves IS from 'intellectuals'; 'over' puts these above M in the down entry. 'minute' looks like tiny, but is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a social blunder or a mistake in grammar, a lapse in correct form.

clue.text: Buzz, possibly, from opiate man supplemented with three rounds gone

indicators.note: gone suggests the letters have gone wild or haywire, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a round is a circle, the shape of the letter O, so three of them give three Os

explanation.surface: An addict gets a high from an opiate dealer whose extra rounds have run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' looks like the drug's high; it is an example of a word that sounds like what it describes. 'supplemented with' adds the three Os before 'gone' shuffles everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz imitates the sound it names, making it a textbook case of words formed by imitation of sound.

clue.text: Interpret Christmas poem?

parts.note: Dec, December, is the month of Christmas
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Work out the meaning of a festive poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas stands for its month, abbreviated DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to work out its meaning, which is to interpret it.

clue.text: Wealth of Roman coins bearing head of Tiberius

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the coins hold the letter within them

parts.note: the as, plural asses, was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Riches in the form of Roman coins stamped with the emperor Tiberius's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' puts T, the 'head of Tiberius', inside ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things of value that a person owns, which together make up their wealth.

clue.text: Journey started in intermittent fashion close to Warwick

indicators.note: intermittent means on and off, so only every other letter of the word is kept
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A trip that began in fits and starts near the town of Warwick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in intermittent fashion' keeps TRE, the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'started'; 'close to' gives K.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey, especially one made on foot.

clue.text: Those eating alfresco favour short topless garments

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to pick something is to choose or favour it

indicators.note: topless means the top is removed, here the first letter

parts.note: knickers are undergarments

explanation.surface: A preference for skimpy tops and short underwear, with a saucy hint of nudity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts PICK to PIC and 'topless' cuts KNICKERS to NICKERS. The saucy reading of 'topless garments' is the distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Picnickers are people having an outdoor meal, which is eating in the open air.

clue.text: Such passages that are often blocked partly in a sale

definitions.text: Such passages that are often blocked

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Corridors often obstructed in part during a shop sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passages that are often blocked' suggests crowded shop aisles; it means the nose's airways, as with a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal passages are the airways inside the nose, often blocked during a cold.

clue.text: It's an endless chore to smile

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a grind is tedious, laborious work

explanation.surface: Having to keep smiling is a never-ending drudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts GRIND to GRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name the broad, toothy facial expression of amusement or pleasure.

clue.text: Streaming out, they aim to settle abroad

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: People pouring out of the country hope to make new lives overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaming out' reads as a crowd leaving, which suits the answer; it is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrants are people leaving their own country to make a permanent home in another.

clue.text: Cake's been eaten, some of us have heard

indicators.note: only for speakers who rhyme the cake with 'gone', so the sound match holds for some of us

parts.note: food that has been eaten is gone; with the 's of the clue it makes 's gone

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the cake has all been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The cake's name is said two ways in Britain, rhyming with 'gone' or with 'cone'; only the first fits, hence 'some of us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small British baked good of flour and butter, often eaten with jam and cream.

clue.text: So-called revolutionary plan I monitor a little

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters read backwards
a little of the phrase means only part of its run of letters is used

explanation.surface: A rebel's plan which I keep a bit of an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes LANIMON from 'plan I monitor' and 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means in name only, as a so-called leader has the title but not the power.

clue.text: Reduces periods receiving energy for nothing

indicators.note: receiving says a new letter is taken into the word
for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: school lessons are timetabled as periods
O, the shape of zero, means nothing
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone cuts down on class periods which come with a dose of energy in place of nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving energy for nothing' swaps the O of LESSONS for E.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen something is to make it smaller, so lessens and reduces are synonyms.
